slides.headline: He was executed for refusing to abandon his faith. Every November 24, Sikhs mark the day he chose it anyway.
Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, was executed in Delhi in November 1675 on the orders of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
slides.body: His martyrdom is commemorated every year on November 24 as Shaheedi Divas - the fixed date set by the Nanakshahi calendar - after he refused to convert and chose execution over abandoning his faith.

slides.headline: He died defending the right of others to practice their own faith, not just his own.
slides.body: Guru Tegh Bahadur's stand is remembered as a defense of religious freedom broadly, not only for Sikhs - a sacrifice made on behalf of people outside his own community who were facing the same pressure to convert.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still draws on the example of someone who paid the ultimate price for someone else's right to believe freely.
slides.body: Shaheedi Divas is marked across India every year as a reminder that religious freedom in India has always had defenders willing to risk everything for it.
